edges.evidence: SCHEMA.md Conventions mandates every new page be added to index.md

layers.name: CANON / Governance
layers.description: Canonical authority over the Atlas Tokens corpus. Defines what is real (the published registry manifest) and how the wiki that documents it must be authored (schema, frontmatter, taxonomy). Everything downstream cites these.

layers.name: SOP — Standard Operating Procedure
layers.description: Umbrella operating doctrine for TCS Atlas: the top-level entity page that names the system (registry + verification + watchdog + audits) and the wiki index that is the mandatory first read for any query. Establishes the procedural frame the rest of the spine works inside.

layers.name: SWK — Standard Work Kit
layers.description: The canonical assets standard work consumes: the resolver's registry (26,748 tokens / 53,317 aliases) and its inverted cross-reference index, plus the wiki entity page that documents the registry. This is the tool kit every WI, checklist, and audit resolves against.

layers.name: WI — Work Instruction
layers.description: Procedural verification work performed against the SWK: the resolver smoke test that proves the kit resolves real tokens, the dated verification report that records the result, and the wiki entity page that documents the verification work itself.

layers.name: Checklist — Watchdog
layers.description: The repeating checklist run by the verification watchdog. Each snapshot is one tick of the periodic check (registry pointer + resolutions map + scan counters) — the same checklist re-applied on a schedule. The wiki watchdog page documents the checklist itself.

layers.name: Action Plan — Audits & Remediation
layers.description: Catch-and-fix actions triggered when the watchdog checklist surfaces a gap. The first BD5 cross-corpus audit flagged TCS/_COMMAND_DEPOT/CANON as missing_graph; the second — same tick — records the remediation that finalized CANON as the fifth M6 corpus. The wiki audits page documents the action loop.

layers.name: LMS — Learning Loop
layers.description: Codified learning surface. The second BD5 audit supersedes the first — a captured immune-system lesson preserved as institutional memory. The wiki SCHEMA enforces that future learnings (new pages) must be added to the index, closing the loop back to CANON.
layers.notes: No nodes in the current corpus exist exclusively at the LMS layer; learning is realized through the supersession relationship between the two BD5 audits (Action Plan layer) and the SCHEMA convention (CANON layer) that mandates index registration of every new page. When formal LMS artifacts (course modules, learning records) are added to atlas_tokens, they will register here.

tour.title: Intro — CANON / Governance
tour.narrative: Start at the top of the stack. ATLAS_TOKEN_REGISTRY.md is the human-readable manifest that names the Atlas Tokens system, declares the resolver contract, and lists the upstream source registries. SCHEMA.md is the wiki authoring law — frontmatter, taxonomy, page thresholds — that every entity page below must obey. These two are the CANON: nothing downstream is legal unless it cites and conforms to them.

key_relationships.why: CANON manifest declares the canonical registry asset that the SWK layer holds.
SCHEMA's conventions section mandates that every new wiki page be registered in the SOP index.

tour.title: SOP — Standard Operating Procedure
tour.narrative: tcs-atlas.md is the SOP: the umbrella entity that names the four subsystems (registry, verification, watchdog, audits) and the order in which an operator engages them. index.md is the procedural entry point — the mandatory first read for any query. Together they answer 'what is this system and how do I approach it' before any actual work begins.

key_relationships.why: Index lists tcs-atlas as the lead entity — the SOP entry path.
SOP delegates downward to the SWK registry entity.

tour.title: SWK — Standard Work Kit
tour.narrative: The kit. atlas_token_registry.json holds 26,748 tokens and 53,317 aliases across atlas/atomics/graphify/legacy/pulse kinds — the canonical asset every downstream layer resolves against. atlas_token_xref.json is its companion: five lookup maps for O(1) resolution. registry.md is the wiki page that documents the kit. If a WI, checklist, or action plan can't be traced back to a token in this kit, it isn't standard work.

key_relationships.why: Xref index points into the canonical registry — the kit is the registry plus its lookup index.
SWK entity points forward to the WI that exercises it.

tour.title: WI — Work Instruction
tour.narrative: The work itself. atlas_token_resolver_smoke_2026-05-11.json is the smoke test — a small set of canonical resolutions (legacy cited tokens, pulse pilot tokens, graphify services) executed against the SWK kit to prove the resolver behaves. atlas_token_verification_2026-05-11.json is the full verification report for the same day: scan counts, resolved tokens, unresolved/missing-artifact lists. verification.md documents the WI procedure. This is where the kit gets exercised under instruction.

key_relationships.why: WI executes against the SWK registry — the work instruction can only run because the kit exists.
The first WI run hands off to the watchdog checklist that will repeat the check periodically.

tour.title: Checklist — Watchdog Cadence
tour.narrative: The WI, repeated. Six watchdog snapshots chained head-to-tail (08:44 → 09:49 → 12:48 → 13:21 → 14:22 → 19:02 Z on 2026-05-11) each capture one tick of the periodic check: registry pointer, resolutions map, scan counters. The 13:21 snapshot records 1,921 citations across 247 files with 495 resolved unique tokens and zero unresolved — the checklist passing. watchdog.md documents the cadence. This is the spine's heartbeat.

key_relationships.why: Watchdog snapshots form a temporal chain — each tick of the checklist references its predecessor.
Every watchdog tick resolves back to the SWK registry — the checklist never drifts from the canonical kit.

tour.title: Action Plan — Catch and Fix
tour.narrative: When the checklist surfaces a gap, the action plan fires. BD5_CROSS_CORPUS_AUDIT_20260511T195752Z.md (19:57:52 Z) attests M6 graphify substrate across five corpora — and flags TCS/_COMMAND_DEPOT/CANON as missing_graph. BD5_CROSS_CORPUS_AUDIT_20260511T195932Z.md (19:59:32 Z, one minute later) records the same-tick remediation: CANON now finalized as the fifth formal M6 corpus (19 nodes / 34 edges / 4 confidence). The action plan was 'add CANON to the substrate' — executed inside the same tick. audits.md documents the action loop.

key_relationships.why: Second audit supersedes first — the action plan's outcome record points back at the gap it closed.

tour.title: LMS — Learning Loop & Cross-Cuts
tour.narrative: Close the loop. The supersession between the two BD5 audits is itself the lesson: a captured immune-system catch-and-fix preserved as institutional memory. SCHEMA.md (back in CANON) enforces the LMS contract by mandating that every new wiki page register in index.md — every lesson learned becomes a new entity, becomes a new SOP entry, becomes new SWK to verify. The spine is a cycle, not a one-way pipe. CANON governs, SOP routes, SWK supplies, WI exercises, Checklist repeats, Action Plan remediates, LMS feeds back into CANON.

key_relationships.why: LMS contract: every learning artifact must be registered in the SOP index — loop closes back into governance.
Action Plan entity links back to SOP umbrella — cross-cut showing the spine is a closed cycle, not a one-way pipe.
